nodes.description: ERC20 token contract held by the timelock; set in constructor.
Address that receives the released tokens; set in constructor.
Timestamp after which the tokens can be released; set in constructor.
Constructor validating releaseTime against block.timestamp and storing token, beneficiary and release time.
View returning the held ERC20 token address.
View returning the configured release timestamp.
Public function that checks block.timestamp >= _releaseTime and transfers the full token balance to the beneficiary.
Block timestamp used as a time gate in the constructor and in release().
External ERC20 transfer of the whole balance to the beneficiary, executed via SafeERC20; can transfer control to an untrusted token contract.
Low-level call inside SafeERC20.callOptionalReturn, bypassing return-data size checks and invoking arbitrary token code.
Constructor parameter holding the ERC20 token address.
Constructor parameter holding the beneficiary address.
Constructor parameter holding the release timestamp.
Local variable holding the token balance of this contract before transfer.

edges.reason: Constructor parameter token is stored into the _token state variable.
Constructor parameter beneficiary is stored into the _beneficiary state variable.
Constructor parameter releaseTime is stored into the _releaseTime state variable.
Constructor requirement compares releaseTime with block.timestamp, making deployment conditional on the miner-controlled timestamp.
release() gate require(block.timestamp >= _releaseTime) depends on the miner-controlled timestamp for authorization of the payout.
release() reads the contract token balance into the amount local variable.
The held token contract _token is queried (balanceOf) to derive amount.
The balance amount is passed as the value argument to safeTransfer.
The beneficiary state variable is passed as the destination of safeTransfer.
The held token _token is the target contract of the safeTransfer external call.
release() performs the external token transfer without any reentrancy guard, so a malicious token can re-enter release before state effects are settled.
safeTransfer routes through SafeERC20.callOptionalReturn which executes a low-level call into the untrusted token contract, giving it control flow.
release() reads the _token state variable to build the transfer.
release() reads the _beneficiary state variable as the payout recipient.
